name: llama-cpp-pack
description: Serving GGUF models on consumer gaming GPUs: build, fit, tune, pre-test, serve.

assumptions.claim: there is a discrete GPU to put layers on
assumptions.resolution: no GPU means the CPU build and models under ~4B; the pack still applies, its numbers do not

assumptions.claim: the GPU is AMD, so the advice is Vulkan-versus-ROCm and -ncmoe
assumptions.resolution: on NVIDIA use the CUDA build and --n-cpu-moe for every -ncmoe example; on Intel use Vulkan

assumptions.claim: the tuning needs at most 8 GiB of VRAM
assumptions.resolution: a smaller card than this will not hold the offload numbers either; start from lcpp-recommend.py

assumptions.claim: 8 GiB is the card this was tuned on, so -ncmoe 26 is the wrong number anywhere else
assumptions.resolution: recompute the offload with lcpp-recommend.py: with more VRAM fewer experts leave the card, and the model may fit whole

assumptions.claim: ROCm does not support this silicon, so Vulkan is correct
assumptions.resolution: if ROCm does support this card, build it and compare: field reports show it beating Vulkan by 30 to 50 percent on RDNA3 and CDNA

assumptions.claim: threads equal physical cores, 6 on the machine this was written on
assumptions.resolution: use this machine's physical count, never its logical count

assumptions.claim: port 8115 is free for a bench server
assumptions.resolution: pick the free port the profile names; the port map is a convention, not a requirement

assumptions.claim: the card is idle before a measurement
assumptions.resolution: stop whatever holds the card; a measurement taken now describes contention, not the model

assumptions.claim: the llama.cpp build has --mmproj and n-cpu-moe
assumptions.resolution: build from current master; without n-cpu-moe a 35B MoE cannot fit a small card

assumptions.claim: system RAM can hold the offloaded experts, about 20 GiB for a 35B Q4
assumptions.resolution: below 24 GiB prefer a smaller quant or model; offload that spills to swap runs at single-digit t/s

assumptions.claim: weights being served live on an internal disk, not a USB drive
assumptions.resolution: move the GGUF to an internal disk before tuning; a USB drive can cost an order of magnitude on prefill

assumptions.claim: the agent's own config points at a live endpoint
assumptions.resolution: point the Hades endpoint at the tuned server and match context_tokens to the served n_ctx

assumptions.claim: vision is wired, since the pack documents it
assumptions.resolution: start hades-vision.service and export HADES_VISION_BIN/_MODEL/_PROJECTOR/_PORT, or add a vision block

claims_to_remeasure.hardware: RX 5700 XT 8 GiB, 19B-A3B hybrid Q4_K_M, -ncmoe 20, 32k ctx q8_0 KV
